title: A2 Writing Quiz 8 — Shopping, Money & Technology

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Have you ever bought anything online?
Have you ever buy anything online?
Did you ever bought anything online?
Have you ever bought anything online yet?
questions.explanation: Present perfect question: Have + subject + past participle: 'Have you ever bought anything online?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have bought this phone two years ago.
I bought this phone two years ago.
I have buy this phone two years ago.
I am buying this phone two years ago.
questions.explanation: A finished time expression ('two years ago') needs past simple, not present perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I was paying at the till when my card stopped working.
I paid at the till when my card was stopping working.
I was pay at the till when my card stopped working.
I paying was at the till when my card stopped working.
questions.explanation: Past continuous (background) + past simple (interruption): 'I was paying... when my card stopped working.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This laptop is cheaper than the other one.
This laptop is more cheap than the other one.
This laptop is cheapest than the other one.
This laptop is cheap than the other one.
questions.explanation: One-syllable adjectives take -er for comparatives: 'cheaper than'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This is the most expensive shop in the mall.
This is the more expensive shop in the mall.
This is expensivest shop in the mall.
This is expensive shop in the mall.
questions.explanation: Long adjectives use 'the most' for superlatives: 'the most expensive shop'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Can I pay by card instead of cash?
Can I paying by card instead of cash?
Can I to pay by card instead of cash?
I can pay by card instead of cash?
questions.explanation: 'Can' is followed by the base form of the verb in requests: 'Can I pay...?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: You should compare prices before buying a new phone.
You should to compare prices before buying a new phone.
You should comparing prices before buying a new phone.
You should compares prices before buying a new phone.
questions.explanation: 'Should' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'should compare'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I must have left my wallet at the shop.
I must have leave my wallet at the shop.
I must has left my wallet at the shop.
I must left my wallet at the shop.
questions.explanation: 'Must have' + past participle expresses a logical past conclusion: 'must have left'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I'm going to update my phone software tonight.
I'm going update my phone software tonight.
I going to update my phone software tonight.
I'm going to updating my phone software tonight.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' + base verb expresses a plan: 'going to update'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If the price drops, I will buy the tablet.
If the price will drop, I buy the tablet.
If the price drops, I buy will the tablet.
If the price dropped, I will buy the tablet.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb: 'If the price drops, I will buy the tablet.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I dislike waiting in long queues.
I dislike to wait in long queues.
I dislike wait in long queues.
I dislike waited in long queues.
questions.explanation: 'Dislike' is followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'dislike waiting'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I forgot bringing my shopping list.
I forgot to bring my shopping list.
I forgot bring my shopping list.
I forgot for bring my shopping list.
questions.explanation: 'Forget' is followed by the infinitive with 'to' when talking about forgetting to do something: 'forgot to bring'.

questions.question: I don't have ___ cash on me right now.
options: many
much
a lot
several
questions.explanation: 'Cash' is uncountable, so use 'much' in negative sentences.

questions.question: There are ___ good deals in this shop today.
options: a little
a few
much
little
questions.explanation: 'Deals' is countable, and 'a few' means 'a small number of'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'rather than'.
options: I prefer paying by card rather than cash.
I prefer paying by card rather than but cash.
Rather than I prefer paying by card cash.
I prefer paying by card, rather than, cash.
questions.explanation: 'Rather than' compares two options: 'by card rather than cash.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I won't buy it even if it's on sale.
I won't buy it even if it will be on sale.
I won't buy it even if was it on sale.
I won't buy it even it's on sale.
questions.explanation: 'Even if' + present simple expresses a hypothetical condition: 'even if it's on sale.'

questions.question: These shoes are ___ sale this week only.
options: on
in
at
for
questions.explanation: 'On sale' is a fixed expression meaning 'available at a reduced price': 'shoes are on sale.'

questions.question: Unfortunately, that model is currently ___ stock.
options: out of
off of
away of
short of
questions.explanation: 'Out of stock' is a fixed expression meaning 'not currently available': 'currently out of stock.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "I need a new charger.")
options: She said that she needs a new charger.
She said that she needed a new charger.
She said that she is needing a new charger.
She said she need a new charger.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, present simple usually shifts to past simple: 'she needed a new charger.'

questions.question: Which is the correct way to start an email to customer support about a faulty product?
options: Hey there,
Dear Customer Support Team,
Yo,
Hiya,
questions.explanation: 'Dear Customer Support Team,' is a suitable formal opening when writing to a company department.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to end a formal complaint email to a company?
options: Yours faithfully,
Catch you later,
Cheers,
Take care,
questions.explanation: 'Yours faithfully,' matches 'Dear Sir/Madam,' or a team name when the recipient's name is unknown.

questions.question: Choose the correct suggestion.
options: Why don't we compare prices online first?
Why we don't compare prices online first?
Why not we compare prices online first?
Why don't we comparing prices online first?
questions.explanation: 'Why don't we' + base verb is used to make a suggestion: 'Why don't we compare...'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines 'This is the shop.' and 'I bought my laptop there.'?
options: This is the shop who I bought my laptop.
This is the shop where I bought my laptop.
This is the shop which I bought my laptop.
This is the shop what I bought my laptop.
questions.explanation: 'Where' is used for places in relative clauses: 'the shop where I bought my laptop.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I rarely buy clothes online.
I buy rarely clothes online.
Rarely I buy clothes online always.
I buy clothes rarely online.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb: 'I rarely buy clothes online.'

questions.question: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
options: Do you know if this store accepts returns?
Do you know does this store accept returns?
Do you know if this store accepts returns.
Do you know, if this store accepts returns?
questions.explanation: Indirect yes/no questions use 'if' with normal word order and end with a question mark.

questions.question: I ___ for a new laptop for weeks, but I still haven't decided.
options: look
have looked
have been looking
looked
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous emphasizes duration of an ongoing action: 'have been looking'.

questions.question: This receipt isn't mine, it's ___.
options: you
your
yours
your's
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun (stands alone, no noun after it): 'it's yours.'

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses sequencing words.
options: First, compare prices. Next, read the reviews. Finally, make the purchase.
First compare prices next read reviews finally make purchase.
Finally compare prices, first read reviews, next make purchase.
Next first compare prices, finally read make purchase.
questions.explanation: Sequencing words 'First,', 'Next,' and 'Finally,' organize steps clearly with commas.

questions.question: Every item in this shop ___ a discount this weekend.
options: have
has
having
are having
questions.explanation: 'Every' takes a singular verb: 'Every item has...'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You haven't paid for this yet, have you?
You haven't paid for this yet, haven't you?
You haven't paid for this yet, did you?
You haven't paid for this yet, have?
questions.explanation: Negative statement + positive tag: 'You haven't paid for this yet, have you?'
